public_rationale: He said fuel for data center gas turbines was going to get much more expensive because of the war-driven gas spike. US data centers burn US gas. EIA's monthly Henry Hub prices show US gas fell after the post. It was $3.62 in February 2026 and stayed between $2.77 and $3.15 from March to September 2026. EIA's October outlook puts February to December 2026 at about $3.09, below the 2025 average of $3.53. Over seven months, which included the April and September oil price peaks, US turbine fuel did not get much more expensive. It got cheaper.
limitations: No deadline was stated; I judged the forecast on the seven months after the post, during the conflict.
Henry Hub is a proxy; local hubs and contract prices for specific data centers may differ.
EIA's February to December figure includes forecast months.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: the fuel cost of running on-site gas turbines at US AI data centers will rise a lot because of the war-driven gas price spike.
US data centers buy US gas, so the right measure is the US benchmark price (Henry Hub), not European or Asian prices.
He gave no deadline. Because he tied the forecast to the current spike, I judge it on the months after the post, through the latest monthly data before the evaluation date (September 2026).
criteria.support_condition: Henry Hub monthly prices after the post rise clearly and lastingly above where they were before the post (February 2026 and the 2025 average).
criteria.contradiction_condition: Henry Hub monthly prices in the six or more months after the post stay flat or fall compared with the months before the post and with 2025.
